newsitem.title: CANADA: CN CEO sees meeting 1997 operating target.
newsitem.headline: CN CEO sees meeting 1997 operating target.

text.p: Canadian National Railway Co Chief Executive Paul Tellier said on Wednesday that he sees the company meeting its key 1997 operating ratio target.

"The first two quarters have come out fairly nicely...I am somewhat confident...that we are well-positioned to achieve the target," Tellier told Reuters after the company released second-quarter results.

CN set an operating ratio target of 83 percent for 1997, compared with the 85 percent achieved in 1996. In the second quarter, CN's operating ratio was 80.8 percent, compared with 84.8 percent a year earlier. Its latest six-months operating ratio was 82.9 percent, versus 86 percent.

Operating ratio measures operating expenses, net of financing charges, as a percentage of revenues. It is a standard for measuring the overall performance of a railway. The lower the ratio, the better the railway's performance.
Some U.S. railways have operating ratios as low as 72 percent, while the average is closer to 80 percent.
Tellier said CN would continue to try to improve the quality of its service, after running its trains on time 86 percent of the time in the second quarter.

"We have got to improve a lot our productivity, in terms of revenue and ton miles per employee. Overall across the board, we are still running about 30 percent behind some of the best U.S. railroads and we have got to improve this," he said.

CN will begin contract negotiations this autumn with unions representing about 17,000 of its 23,644 employees. Tellier said CN had to improve its productivity because although profits were up, the company was not returning its cost of capital.
"It's going to be tough negotiations, but I am confident that we will able to make some progress on our agenda -- it's essential," he said.
(On) Wednesday, CN shares were off 0.25 to 67.10 in Toronto on almost 195,000 shares.
